messages.subject: skinwet argument in NicheMapR::ectotherm
messages.body_plain:
Hello NicheMappers,

Does anyone have information on how to parameterise the 'skinwet' argument in the ectotherm model? The documentation describes the parameter as "% of surface area acting as a free-water exchanger, for computing cutaneous water loss". The problem I'm facing is that, of the small number of studies I've found which directly investigate water loss in lizards, none present the % surface area in any results (or even mention it). Common measures are usually mass-specific water loss rate (mg/g/h) or as % body weight per hour. I have been thinking about possible ways to convert existing measures in the literature but it's proving difficult and, I suspect, probably not an ideal solution.

Any insight into this would be great. Thanks in advance!

Simon

messages.subject: Re: skinwet argument in NicheMapR::ectotherm
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

Good question. You can find some of the details in Appendix D to:

Kearney, M., and Porter, W. P. (2004). Mapping the fundamental niche: physiology, climate, and the distribution of a nocturnal lizard. Ecology 85, 3119–3131.

I've attached it to this reply.

Elia Pirtle and I have an almost-ready R function for making estimates of this parameter from different sorts of evaporative water loss data which we'll include in the NicheMapR package, if you can wait a bit. We will likely sort this out by early Nov.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Microclimate in future climates?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

This is probably a stupid question: is there a microclimate model for future climates? If so, can someone please kindly point me in the right direction for implementing it?
Thanks if so,
Jenn

messages.subject: Re: Microclimate in future climates?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jenn,

It's a matter of adding the appropriate temperature, rainfall, etc. offsets to the base climatology you're using, in the function you're using to run the microclimate model, so it runs off those adjusted forcing variables. I haven't yet collated one to go with the New et al. 2002 climate data. I have for Australia and New Zealand. You can't run the micro_aust or micro_nz functions without access to the requisite data sets but you can look at the code in those functions for generating the climate change scenarios and emulate that with a global climate change scenario.

All the best,
Mike
